$comment: requirements.example.json: the REVIEWED expectations for the fictional 'Example' build in templates/font.example.json (review finding F002). Write this file at the guideline phase and change it only with the operator. scripts/tests/test_font.py compares the built fonts against THIS file, never against font.json, so a font.json edit that lowers a floor, drops an axis or drops a character goes red here. Every key is explained in references/variable-font-build.md ('requirements.json, key by key').
$comment_word_space: word_space pins the word-space advance per master, in units, as the operator reviewed it (review finding C9); the test holds the built font AND a fresh export to it, so the exporter's own figure is never its own expectation. These are the values export.js lays for this example's concepts (210 + 0.3 W + 2 track), read once from the export.
$comment_cmap: cmap is EXACTLY the set of characters the built font maps: every glyph key the generator draws (gen.js G, which includes the standing symbols copyright, bullet and trade mark) plus the builder's quote and space glyphs. It is therefore a superset of required_characters, which lists only what the site's titles need; the three symbols are mapped because the generator draws them for every project, not because this example's titles use them.
titles: A Short Walk to the Weir
$comment_tables: tables pins the font-table decisions build.py makes by default. prep_hex is the smart-dropout program (PUSHW 0x01FF, SCANCTRL, PUSHB 4, SCANTYPE) that pairs with the gasp above; code_page_range1 is OS/2 ulCodePageRange1 (bit 0, Latin 1); mac_names false means the name table has no Macintosh (platform 1) records. names.fs_type is the embedding permission and is the operator's decision: 0 installable (an open face), 4 Preview & Print (the usual setting for a proprietary face), 2 Restricted (some tools refuse the font); browsers ignore it for web fonts. vertical_metrics (per group) is the reviewed line height: hhea and OS/2 typo carry these numbers with a line gap of 0, win covers every glyph; read them from the first build's `vertical metrics written` self-check line and review them, because they decide `line-height: normal`.
$comment_qa: accepted_qa_findings: every FontBakery FAIL or ERROR the project accepts, each with its reason (scripts/fontbakery-gate.py). Start with [] and add an entry only after reading the finding; `codes` (optional) limits the accepted FontBakery message codes, so a new kind of failure of the same check blocks; without it the match is the check id alone and the reason names what was seen. A deliberate non-zero fsType is accepted under the vendor profiles' check id, googlefonts/fstype, with the licence as the reason. The generator draws lowercase ì î ò ù û ā š with no uppercase counterpart, which FontBakery's case_mapping fails; the example accepts it:

accepted_qa_findings.reason: the generator's glyph set has the lowercase ì î ò ù û ā š and not Ì Î Ò Ù Û Ā Š (seven pairs, listed in FontBakery's message); a capital is a new skeleton, which is a generator change

the roman and the italic file carry no `ital` axis in STAT (FontBakery wants ital 0, elidable and linked to 1, in the roman and ital 1 in the italic, so a font picker can pair the two files); the build does not write it because the roman's STAT would then depend on whether an italic group exists, and browsers do not read STAT; a later change to build.py
the example's italic is a one-axis group (wght) beside a two-axis roman (wght and opsz), which is the shape it exists to exercise; FontBakery expects every file of a family to carry the same axes
the same fact as family_axis_ranges: the italic file has no opsz axis (FontBakery: lacks a 'opsz' variation axis)

each group measures its own glyph extent (the roman 957, the italic 956 units), and the two files are built one at a time, so build.py cannot give both the family's maximum; typo_metrics would equalise hhea and typo but not the measured win metrics; a later change to build.py
